title: Astrometry.net Solve Failure Rate
dataSources: Observatory environment (`observatory:env`), sky-quality meter (`skyquality:reading`), imaging sessions (`imaging:session`), telescope mount (`mount:status`), cloud sensor (`allsky:cloud`).
app: Backyard observatory automation — roll-off-roof/dome controller, sky-quality meter, cloud sensor, telescope mount, and astrophotography software (N.I.N.A./Ekos) — via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=astrometry:solve
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(solve_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by target_name
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often Astrometry.net solve records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each target.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize solve_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per target.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It reviews which parts of your Astrometry.net solve data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
